Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Regional Bono East Regional Minister reaffirms gov’t commitment to infrastructure and job creation at Offuman Fofie Yam Festival Source : Anass Sabit 21 November 2026 5:05pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Bono East Regional Minister, Francis Owusu Antwi, joined the Paramount Chief of the Offuman Traditional Area, Nana Kwaku Gyan Borokuo II, for the grand durbar of the Offuman Traditional Council’s 2026 Annual Fofie Yam Festival, where he reaffirmed the government's commitment to improving infrastructure and creating jobs.
The vibrant celebration served as a significant platform for the Regional Minister to engage with traditional leadership and the people of Offuman, while showcasing the government’s ongoing developmental interventions in the area and across the Bono East Region.
In his address, Mr Antwi outlined several key projects aimed at boosting the local economy and improving livelihoods. A major highlight was the new cashew processing factory at Tuobodom, which is expected to create employment opportunities for approximately 1,500 people.
The Minister also noted the construction of the critical Offuman–Wenchi and Offuman–Amoma roads, as well as the construction of six-unit classroom blocks at Offuman and Issahkrom, alongside several other ongoing projects.
“I reaffirmed the government’s commitment to improving infrastructure, creating jobs, expanding educational opportunities, and improving the livelihoods of our people,” the Minister stated.
Addressing the gathering, the Offumanhene, Nana Kwaku Gyan Borokuo II, called for continued unity among his people and appealed to the government to extend development projects to the area.
“Peace and unity are the foundation upon which every meaningful development is built. I urge all my people to embrace peace and work together, and I call on the government to remember Offuman and bring more development to our area,” the Offumanhene stated.
The Regional Minister also commended the Offuman Traditional Council for preserving the region's rich cultural heritage and using the annual festival as a platform to promote unity, peace, and development.
The event was graced by a high-powered entourage, including 10 out of the 11 Municipal and District Chief Executives (MDCEs) across the Bono East Region, demonstrating a unified front for regional development.
Together, the leadership reaffirmed their dedication to building a stronger and more prosperous Bono East Region.
